text.p: Bear Stearns on Monday initiated coverage of Mexico's second largest steel maker Hylsamex with an attractive rating and a 12-month price target of $31/ADR.

"Our investment thesis is based on a rebound of steel demand in Mexico...and on the company's involvement in several projects to increase volume sales, add more value to its products and control costs," analyst Marco Soligo wrote in a report.
Soligo said the most important projects the Monterrey-based company has in the pipeline include a phase two expansion of the company's flat products minimill that will double capacity.
Also, Hyslamex plans to lower costs through a new 700,000 tonne DRI reactor and focus on higher value added products through the expansion of several production lines.

"Altogether, net revenues should increase 19 percent between 1996-1999, the operating margin should rise to 25 percent in 1999 from 18 percent in 1997 and operating cash flow per ADR should jump 52 percent, to $1.71 per ADR in 1999 from $1.12 per ADR in 1997," Soligo wrote.

Bear Stearns said it expects Hylsamex to suffer equity dilution since the company has already announced it will make a small equity offering to help finance current investment plans. "We estimate the shareholder base will expand to 260.8 million from 244 million shares, with an impact of $0.10 per ADR on 1997 earnings," Soligo said.
